summary.title: Approach: Building a toy template engine in Python
summary.one_liner: You learn how a simple template engine works internally by building one in Python, covering tokenizing with regular expressions, an AST of nodes, scope handling, and rendering with context resolution.
takeaways: Templates can be split into text, variable and block fragments using a regex with split().
A compiler builds an AST of node objects, with scope-creating nodes managed by a stack during compilation.
Rendering walks the AST, using ast.literal_eval to distinguish literals from context names.
Dotted names and '..' parent-context references are resolved by walking nested dictionaries.
summary.summary: The article walks through a deliberately simple template language with variables, each loops, if/else conditionals, and callable tags. It explains the theory of ASTs, then implements tokenizing with a non-greedy regular expression and split(). The compile step uses a Node base class with process_fragment, enter_scope, exit_scope and render methods, plus a scope stack. Rendering uses ast.literal_eval and a resolver for dotted and parent-context names. The author notes the code is academic, not production quality.
